title: HMAC buffers entire input before hardware dispatch: O(input) heap for bulk HMAC
description:
The accumulation buffer in Crypto2DevHmacCtx grows unbounded: every wc_HmacUpdate appends to a heap buffer that is flushed in one write() at Final time.

For TLS record MACs (max ~16 KB), this allocates 16 KB per in-flight HMAC. At 10 Gbps with many sessions, this is modest.

For any non-TLS caller using bulk HMAC (e.g., file integrity over GB-scale input), memory usage is proportional to the HMAC input size. A 1 GB file HMAC would hold 1 GB in the process heap during computation.

Expected impact at scale: Memory pressure on bulk-data use cases. The comment documents this and suggests using a separate devId that skips HMAC offload for bulk data. That workaround is correct but requires the user to understand the HMAC batching design.

Root cause: crypto2dev device has no stateful streaming HMAC fd (no multiple-write-then-final protocol). The buffering is intrinsic to the device design, not a port choice.
